title: Nilpotence of an element in a residue fibre is detected by the characteristic polynomial
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a ring map whose target is finite free of rank n as a module, an element acts nilpotently on the fibre at a prime exactly when that prime contains the first n coefficients of the characteristic polynomial (statement lines 5771-5783). The proof does not use determinants of the action on generators: it compares the fibre characteristic polynomial with the reduction of the given one, applies Cayley-Hamilton on both sides, and reads the condition off the coefficients (proof lines 5785-5812). Reducing modulo the prime so that the two polynomials agree is the step that carries the argument. H2.
